docs.title: Star-Allele-Search
docs.text:
Welcome to the Star-Allele-Search documentation.

Star-Allele-Search is a tool for retrieving, validating and annotating pharmacogenomic star allele information using data from:

  • PharmVar
  • ClinPGx
  • CPIC
  • DPWG

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Star allele lookup
  • PharmVar integration
  • Clinical guideline annotations
  • Phenotype information retrieval
  • Pharmacogenomic reporting

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: See the Installation guide to set up the project locally.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Star-Allele-Search can be installed in two ways:

  1. Local installation using a Python virtual environment.
  2. Docker installation using a pre-built container.

Choose the method that best suits your environment.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or later
  • Git
  • Internet connection for downloading dependencies

For containerised deployment, Docker is required.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Star-Allele-Search is a pharmacogenomics application developed to retrieve, validate and annotate pharmacogenomic star allele information.

The application integrates information from multiple external resources, including PharmVar and ClinPGx, to provide allele-specific information, phenotype annotations and clinical guideline recommendations.

docs.text:

Guideline Retrieval

Results

docs.title: pharmvar_json.py
docs.text:
Responsible for retrieving star allele information from the PharmVar API.

Main responsibilities include:

  • Connecting to PharmVar
  • Retrieving allele definitions
  • Parsing JSON responses
  • Formatting allele information

docs.title: fetch_guidelines.py
docs.text:
Responsible for retrieving pharmacogenomic guideline information.

Main responsibilities include:

  • Connecting to ClinPGx resources
  • Retrieving guideline annotations
  • Parsing recommendation data

docs.text: Processes ClinPGx annotations and generates structured summaries.

docs.text: Validates gene names using HGNC nomenclature.

docs.title: vv_validation.py
docs.text: Performs validation checks on user input prior to processing.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Automated testing is implemented using PyTest.

Tests are stored in the repository test directory.

docs.title: Run Tests
docs.text: pytest

docs.title: Run Coverage
docs.text:
pytest --cov=App

Coverage reports are used to assess the effectiveness of the automated test suite.

Both happy-path and exception handling behaviour are tested.

docs.title: Continuous Integration
docs.text:
GitHub Actions is used to automate project testing.

The workflow performs the following tasks:

  1. Creates a clean environment.
  2. Installs project dependencies.
  3. Executes the automated test suite.
  4. Generates coverage metrics.
  5. Reports build success or failure.

Documentation is automatically deployed using GitHub Pages.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Logging is used throughout the application to record operational events and errors.

Log levels include:

  • DEBUG
  • INFO
  • WARNING
  • ERROR

Logs can be used to troubleshoot API failures and unexpected behaviour.

docs.title: Exception Handling
docs.text:
The application uses exception handling to ensure failures are reported gracefully.

Examples include:

  • Invalid user input
  • Network failures
  • API errors
  • JSON parsing failures

Exceptions are logged to aid debugging and maintenance.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Star-Allele-Search is a pharmacogenomics application that retrieves, validates and annotates star allele information from multiple external resources.

Figure 1. Homepage

The application combines information from:

  • PharmVar
  • ClinPGx
  • CPIC
  • DPWG

to provide clinically relevant pharmacogenomic information.

docs.title: Typical Workflow
docs.text:
The user provides a star allele query.

CYP2C19*2

The application:

  1. Retrieves allele information from PharmVar.
  2. Validates gene and allele information.
  3. Retrieves phenotype information.
  4. Retrieves associated pharmacogenomic guidelines.
  5. Generates an annotated result.
User Input
     │
     ▼
 Star Allele Query
     │
     ▼
 PharmVar Retrieval
     │
     ▼
 Phenotype Mapping
     │
     ▼
 Guideline Retrieval
     │
     ▼
 Results

docs.title: Example Search
docs.text:
The following example shows a search for CYP2C19*2(UPDATE CLOSER TO SUBMISSION).

Figure 2. Example search for CYP2C192.*

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text:
CYP2C19*2

The query should contain:

  • A valid gene name
  • A valid star allele designation

Example valid inputs:

CYP2C19*2
CYP2D6*4
SLCO1B1*5
TPMT*3A

docs.title: Understanding the Results
docs.text: The application may return several categories of information.

docs.title: Star Allele Information
docs.text:
Example:

Gene: CYP2C19
Allele: *2
Function: No Function

This information is retrieved from PharmVar.

docs.title: Phenotype Information
docs.text:
Example:

Phenotype:
Poor Metaboliser

Phenotype predictions are generated from available pharmacogenomic annotations.

docs.title: Clinical Guidelines
docs.text:
The application retrieves available recommendations from sources such as:

  • CPIC
  • DPWG

Example:

Drug: Clopidogrel

Recommendation:
Consider an alternative antiplatelet agent in patients with reduced CYP2C19 function.

docs.title: Clinical Interpretation
docs.text:
The application can be used to identify clinical recommendations associated with pharmacogenomic variants.

Examples:

  • Clopidogrel and CYP2C19
  • Simvastatin and SLCO1B1
  • Thiopurines and TPMT

docs.title: Research and Validation
docs.text:
Researchers can use the software to:

  • Validate allele nomenclature
  • Retrieve allele definitions
  • Compare annotations across resources
  • Review published recommendations

docs.title: Allele Not Found
docs.text:
Example:

No results returned

Possible causes:

  • Incorrect gene symbol
  • Incorrect star allele designation
  • Allele not present in the data source

Verify the allele using PharmVar.

docs.title: API Connection Errors
docs.text:
Example:

Failed to retrieve PharmVar data

Possible causes:

  • Network connectivity problems
  • Invalid API credentials
  • Temporary service outage

Check internet connectivity and API configuration.

docs.text:
